# Docker-style argument mapping

Finch translates docker-style arguments into the arguments of the container
runtime it drives. When `dockercompat: true` is set in `finch.yaml`, the
translation applies to `run`, `create`, `exec`, and `build`.

<!-- This file is generated by pkg/argtranslate/gen. Do not edit it by hand. -->

## Categories

Every argument falls into exactly one category.

| Category | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pass` | Forwarded unchanged, with the same name and value. |
| `rewrite` | Renamed or given a fixed replacement value, then forwarded. |
| `special` | The value needs sub-command aware surgery (path mapping, `consistency=` removal, `host-gateway` resolution, `--cpu-quota 0`) before forwarding. |
| `ignored` | Accepted but not forwarded; a warning names the flag. The rationale column states why dropping it is harmless. |
| `unsupported` | Rejected before the runtime runs. Every unsupported flag is reported in one error. |

| `--secret` | value, repeatable | `special` | same flag, value rewritten as `id=ID,src=PATH` | expects `id=ID,src=PATH` |
| `--security-opt` | value, repeatable | `unsupported` | rejected | docker legacy builder option; the runtime's build has no equivalent |
| `--shm-size` | value | `unsupported` | rejected | docker legacy builder option; the runtime's build has no equivalent |
| `--source-policy-file` | value | `pass` | same flag | runtime extension; docker does not define it, forwarded unchanged |
| `--squash` | bool | `unsupported` | rejected | docker legacy builder option; the runtime's build has no equivalent |
| `--ssh` | value, repeatable | `pass` | same flag | runtime extension; docker does not define it, forwarded unchanged |
| `--tag, -t` | value, repeatable | `pass` | same flag | - |
| `--target` | value | `pass` | same flag | - |
| `--ulimit` | value, repeatable | `unsupported` | rejected | docker legacy builder option; the runtime's build has no equivalent |

## Arguments that change behaviour

These arguments used to be forwarded or dropped silently. They are listed here
because the change is visible to existing scripts.

| Argument | Sub-command | Before | After | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--kernel-memory` | run, create | forwarded unchanged; the runtime logs that the flag is a no-op | accepted, dropped with a warning that names the flag | scripts keep running; the warning now makes the lost limit visible |
| `consistency= inside --mount` | run | deleted silently and the remaining keys reordered by a map round-trip | deleted with a warning that names --mount and the dropped key; the remaining keys keep their order | scripts keep running; the command line becomes stable and the loss is visible |
| `--expose, --publish-all, --link, --network-alias, --net-alias, --storage-opt, --volume-driver` | run, create | forwarded and rejected later by the runtime with "unknown flag" | rejected by finch before the runtime runs, all at once, with a doc link | the command already failed; only the message and the timing change |
| `everything else classified unsupported` | all | forwarded and rejected later by the runtime one flag at a time | rejected by finch with every unsupported flag in one error | the command already failed; the fix is now a single round-trip |

### Lenient mode

Setting `dockercompat_lenient: true` in `finch.yaml` turns an unsupported
argument into a warning and drops it, so a script that relied on a flag being
ignored keeps running. It is off by default.

* Strict (default): one error lists every unsupported flag with the
  sub-command and a link to this page. Old scripts break, but the failure is
  complete and actionable.
* Lenient: old scripts keep running, but a dropped argument can look applied
  when it is not. Every drop is warned about by name.

## Runtime defaults differ

For these arguments, forwarding only what the user wrote cannot reproduce
docker's behaviour, so the translator supplies a default.

| Argument | Sub-commands | Docker default | Runtime default | What finch does | Effect on existing users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--platform` | run, create, build | defaults to the DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM environment variable | has no environment-based default | finch injects --platform=$DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM when the variable is set and the flag is absent | users who set the variable only get the docker behaviour now; users who do not set it see no change |
| `--cpu-quota` | run, create | 0 means unset | -1 means unset and 0 means a zero quota | an explicit --cpu-quota 0 is rewritten to --cpu-quota -1 | only users who passed 0 explicitly are affected, and they get the docker meaning back |

## Where path conversion happens

The translator decides *which* values are host paths and *what* to strip. It
never knows how to convert them: the mapping is injected through
`PathMapper.MapHostPath` and `HostGatewayResolver.ResolveHostGateway`. On
macOS the mapper is the identity, because the host home directory is mounted
into the VM at the same path. On Windows it maps a drive letter to
`/mnt/<drive>`. Because the legacy per-argument handlers are bypassed once
translation is active, a path is converted exactly once.

Values mapped as host paths: the `-v`/`--volume` source, a `type=bind`
`--mount` source, `--label-file`, `--cidfile`, `--cosign-key`, and the build
`-f`/`--file`, `--iidfile`, `--output dest=`, `--secret src=`,
`--cache-from`, `--cache-to`, `--build-context`, and the build context.

### Environment files

`--env-file` is forwarded with its path mapped, and the runtime reads the file
inside the VM. The translator never opens the file. One consequence: a line
that names a variable without a value is resolved against the environment
inside the VM, whereas docker resolves it on the host. Use an explicit
`-e NAME` if the host value is the one you want; that case is resolved on the
host and forwarded as `NAME=value`.

## Not covered

`compose`, `inspect`, `cp`, and `save`/`load` keep their existing handlers and
are not part of this matrix.
